skills.stdout_tail:
- VI. THE TRACE - the exact integer the ratio is measuring against ------
Pisot's bound is |lambda**n - p_n| <= 2 |alpha|**n, where p_n is the
sum of the n-th powers of all the roots and is an integer.  The scan
measures |lambda**n - round(lambda**n)|, so the two agree only where
round(lambda**n) is p_n.  For small n the conjugate term is still
above one half and it is not, and those n are reported here.

  tribonacci  p_0..p_6 [3, 1, 3, 7, 11, 21, 39]
              round(lambda**n) != p_n at [1, 3]
              the trace is the nearest integer from n = 4 up, 198 of 200 terms

  plastic     p_0..p_6 [3, 0, 2, 3, 2, 5, 5]
              round(lambda**n) != p_n at [1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9]
              the trace is the nearest integer from n = 10 up, 194 of 200 terms

Neither base has a clean sweep, and the two fail at different n.
A ratio computed over n <= 200 that claims to be the Pisot error
is therefore wrong at a handful of terms, and at n = 1 it is wrong
by a factor of five.  The bound still holds everywhere; it is the
identification of the numerator with the Pisot error that fails.

The two bases disagree about how bad this is: tribonacci is clean
from n = 4, plastic only from n = 10, and plastic is the base whose
maximum sits closer to the bound.  A tighter bound is not a more
trustworthy one, and the two findings have to be read together.
